_metered._how: Photo boxes are hand-placed on clean single-material patches at NATIVE 1200x1600 (scratchpad/bsmt/m2.py reports mean, sd, mean|d1| between adjacent pixels and |d1|/sd together). Render walls are metered by the DIFF-MASK method (scratchpad/bsmt/probe2.py): the room is rendered with one wall's skin changed and the pixels that moved ARE that wall, so no sample box can swallow a cabinet. Render floor/rug numbers come from the top-down plan pose. NOTE the photos are a NIGHT shot under RGB cove/hex fixtures -- every surface is colour-cast and the absolute luminances are NOT comparable to a daylight render; ratios and texture statistics are. ALSO note round 2's four wall numbers are void: the south 'wall' it metered was the Movie Room's wall face (see _round3.bug_found_and_fixed), and all four skins have been re-solved from scratch this round.

At #fafafa the four walls render N 235.3 / E 185.8 / S 160.2 / W 213.5; at #6e6e6e they render N 165.2 / E 73.2 / S 50.6 / W 105.3. Two-point power fits (gamma N 0.431, E 1.135, S 1.403, W 0.861) inverted for a common target of 170 gave albedos 118 / 231 / 255 / 192, which rendered 173.1 / 173.9 / 162.6 / 182.9; one measured nudge plus a 1.5% warm shift gives the values below.

Measured 30.8-34.0% at the contact edge over 0.82 ft.

_round4.scope: CABINET ARTWORK ONLY.  No room geometry, no footprints, no app code, no other room, no poses.json.  Every z/x position, width, height, deck height, marquee depth, plinth and profile style in ar2.py's three run tables is round 3's, unchanged.
_round4.the_defect: Round 3's critic: 'the cabinet artwork is one machine repeated sixteen times in different hues, where the photograph shows four unrelated printed graphics.'  Correct. a2kit._art_atlas() painted 16 tiles of which 0-11 were the SAME motif (ground gradient + header strip + one off-centre blob) in twelve hues and 12-15 were sine-wash bands with rectangles standing in for lettering.  upright() then fed ONE of those tiles to the front panel AND the control deck AND the screen bezel.
_round4.the_fix: 16 machines identified from the owner's photographs and drawn individually by four art modules (scratchpad/arc4/art/art_g0..3.py), packed by scratchpad/arc4/atlas4.py into one atlas PER WALL RUN, and wired by slug in ar2.py.  Each machine now has its own .marquee / .side / .front / .deck, its own marquee emissive tint, and its own carcase / T-molding colour.

atlas.why_three: glb.py shares an image by byte identity INSIDE one file, but Cabinets East / North / South are three GLBs, so one room-wide atlas is paid for three times.
atlas.supersample: every panel painted at 2x and box-averaged down; art_g2 paints into a fixed 256 buffer and point-samples on the way out, which shreds letterforms at any smaller tile.
atlas.quantisation: 16 levels/channel after the average.  The modules quantise to 8 and lean on a fixed 4x4 Bayer pattern; box-averaging destroys both and cost 0.86 bytes/px against their own 0.13-0.47.  Re-quantising put it back: 243.2 KB at 8 levels, 174.9 at 16, for the same panel sizes.  Re-dithering at quantise time cost 40 KB and was rejected.

_round4.marquee_emissive: A marquee IS a backlit lamp in the photographs, so it stays emissive -- a fixture the photograph shows, at the size it shows it, which is the exception ROOM-BRIEF allows.  Round 3 shared four pastels across sixteen machines at strength 1.7.  Now per-machine (a2kit.MARQUEE): hue from that band, value LOW, strength ~1.  glTF emissive is a flat factor with no texture, so the first pass at the band's own light hue washed NBA Jam's crimson caps pink and bleached the Turtles marquee; the shipped tints sit at luma 60-85 for the bands the photos show LIT (Pac-Man, NBA Jam, Time Crisis, Golden Tee, Ridge Racer) and 22-30 for the ones they show dark (Star Wars, NFL Blitz, the graffiti multicade, east-7).
_round4.carcase_colour: New this round (a2kit.CARCASE).  sweep()'s perimeter quads are the cabinet's top, back and the strip of front face either side of the printed panel -- i.e. the T-molding.  Round 3 painted all sixteen black.  Now: Star Wars and Pac-Man yellow carcases, Turtles bright grass-green molding, Time Crisis and Ridge Racer red bodies, MK / NBA Jam / T2 maroon molding, Marvel Super Heroes gold-tan.  Material colour only, no geometry.
declared: EAST_RUN[6] is kept because this round changed artwork, not layout, and the geometry was explicitly out of scope.  The roster counted FIVE uprights on the east wall in four independent frames, not seven, so the slot is dressed as an honest unbranded black upright with a blank marquee and no licensed graphic.  It should be DELETED and the run re-spaced in a geometry round.

No riser quads were added.  art_g1 and art_g2 painted separate .riser panels for Marvel Super Heroes, Turtles and Marvel vs Capcom, but the cabinet has no riser geometry and splitting the front quad would squash those machines' front artwork ~20% vertically.  Marvel vs Capcom therefore carries its wordmark on the printed base band of its front panel rather than on a separate riser; the roster says that machine's own lower front is 'essentially no printed graphic'.
time-crisis.speaker was painted by art_g1 and is NOT packed -- the cabinet has no separate speaker quad.

Three of art_g3's four bezels are dropped (its own assessment: they 'carry no identity').  Golden Tee's is kept because its lit yellow three-panel instruction strip is a real feature.  The other fifteen bezels are a plain untextured #15151a material, per art_g0's recommendation -- round 3 reused the front tile there, which smeared NBA Jam's flaming ball round its monitor.

sweep() maps ONE side rect to both flanks, so a machine's side art is correctly anchored to the cabinet on both sides but reads mirrored on the +x flank.  Not fixed: fixing it needs a second, mirrored tile per machine, and only Star Wars and the graffiti multicade have side art with any directional content.

The display case's 30 collectible boxes (NE corner) take a rotation of the NORTH run's own panels (ar2.BOX_ART).  They are 0.35 x 0.58 ft boxes seen from across the room, so what they need is varied printed colour, not identity -- but a critic is entitled to know they are cabinet artwork re-used at box scale.

flip=True was removed from the control-deck quad.  It mirrored the tile left-right, which was harmless on an abstract motif and is not now: NBA Jam's logo lies on its boards, Golden Tee's deck legend is three words, Mortal Kombat's carries its wordmark.

The four judged poses in shoot4.py all aim DOWN and crop every machine at the screen bezel, so not one marquee was in shot.  Four level frames at marquee height were ADDED (mq_east, mq_north, mq_south, mq_south_w); the original four are unchanged so the A/B against base_*.png still holds.

payload.note: Round 3's whole art atlas was 29.3 KB because it was twelve hues of one drawing.  Sixteen machines' worth of real artwork at 256 px would be ~1.2 MB per copy and ~3.6 MB across the three GLBs.  Per-run atlases, per-panel-class sizes and 16-level re-quantisation land it at 163.1 KB total.

_round5.scope: Arcade Room cabinet artwork + control hardware. Integration of four parallel art modules (art_g0..art_g3) into the packed atlases and into ar2.upright().
_round5.why: Three independent critics failed round 4 with the same sentence: every cabinet wore one recoloured asset - the same centred grey coin-door rectangle, the same two-joystick deck (one red top, one blue top) over the same row of flat square buttons, and a blurry floated word as the only per-title differentiation. The paint half of the fix was done by four wrap agents; the geometry half was four dicts nobody read.

changed.scratchpad/arc4/atlas4.py: ISOTROPIC RECTANGULAR PACKING. SIZE[cls] is now a scale, not a tile edge: a panel of world aspect A packs at S*sqrt(A) x S/sqrt(A). A 3.4:1 marquee went from 120x120 (55 px/ft across) to 188x55 (85 px/ft across) - fewer bytes AND 57% more resolution where letterforms run. art_g1's paint functions carry a native non-square .rect() and are handed the real shape; art_g0/g2/g3 keep the unchanged square contract and are area-averaged into the rectangle. Also: per-panel aspects pushed in from ar2 (the only module that knows the real geometry), art_g2.LEGACY_PANELS folded in as a fallback so east-7-no-machine keeps round 4's unbranded panels, and six EXTRA_KEYS added (marvel-super-heroes.bezel and the four south .screen panels).
changed.scratchpad/arc4/decks5.py: NEW. Normalises the four art modules' mutually incompatible deck and coin-door schemas into one. They disagreed on the coordinate frame (u -0.5..0.5 / -1..1 / 0..1), on radius vs diameter, on every field name, and on how 'no door' is spelled (None / [] / proud 0.0). Nothing is dropped silently; SKIPPED names the two items that are not built and why.
changed.scratchpad/bsmt/ar2.py: upright() now reads decks5: per-machine buttons, sticks, ball and bat tops, two trackballs, a spinner, four light guns, a Star Wars flight yoke, a Ridge Racer steering wheel, a lit front-lip strip, and 0/1/2 coin doors per machine at that machine's own size, colour and place. Front-panel rect is per-machine (art_g2's four run to the floor). Four south screens carry printed panels. All hardware is VERTEX-COLOURED on two shared materials.
changed.scratchpad/bsmt/a2kit.py: DECK_MAT gained six rows (all requested by the module that drew the deck - ART_DK #4c4c4c was crushing the hardwood court, the fairway, the ice-blue lightning field and the violet nebula), and a new SCREEN material for the printed south monitors.

hardware_built.note: Round 4 built two joysticks and six flat squares on all sixteen machines and one identical grey coin plate. No two decks in the room now share a control count, a colour, a button size or a stick top.

levers_taken: isotropic packing: -52.7 KB against the same art packed square
vertex-coloured hardware on 2 materials instead of ~44 per run: -68 KB (a glTF primitive costs ~0.9 KB of accessors and JSON before a triangle is in it; COLOR_0 costs 4 bytes a vertex)
coin-slot / return-cup / door-bezel relief as single quads instead of boxes: -36 KB, and every one of them is drawn into the printed artwork at the same coordinates anyway
QUANT 16 -> 20: -14.2 KB, no banding visible at panel scale
SIZE[side] 58 -> 42 for the occluded flanks: -3 KB
levers_refused: QUANT 24 (-15 KB more): round 4 measured 24 as where banding starts on a marquee, the hero surface
cutting any machine's artwork: ROOM-BRIEF forbids deleting content to hit a number, and it was not needed
payload.negative_result: Per-row adaptive PNG filtering (Sub/Up/Average/Paeth by the spec's minsum heuristic) was implemented and MEASURED 14% WORSE on these atlases: 158.1 KB filter-0 vs 180.5 KB adaptive. These are synthetic flat graphics whose identical rows zlib matches wholesale; a per-row predictor destroys those matches. Recorded in atlas4.py so nobody tries it again.

_round6_guns.scope: The four LIGHT GUNS on terminator-2 and time-crisis, and the holsters they stand in. Nothing else in the room was touched.
_round6_guns.defect: Round 5 built each gun as three flat-shaded boxes -- a coloured body box on a darker grip box on a plate -- so from every judged south pose the pair read as a red slab and a blue slab standing on a white pedestal (scratchpad/arc4/shots/r5b_mq_south.png, r5b_full_south.png). The plate metered 212 grey against a 73 deck because the a2hw hardware material is roughness 0.42 and its up-facing top blew out on the ceiling cans, not because its authored colour was wrong (#181521).

built.geometry: One CONCAVE side profile per gun -- backstrap, receiver, a step down to the barrel, the muzzle, the frame, the trigger guard's front and bottom straps, the recess behind them and a raked grip -- pushed across the gun's width, plus a U-channel holster socket under the butt. `prism()` could not build the profile: its caps are a triangle fan from vertex 0, which folds over on a concave outline, so ar2 now ear-clips them (`_earclip`/`_extrude`, new).
built.profile: ar2._GUN_PROFILE, 13 points normalised to gun length; ar2._GUN_PITCH 12 deg nose-up.
built.two_tone: grip colour on profile points 10-12 and 0, body colour on the rest, as COLOR_0 -- no extra material, no extra primitive.
built.shading: Split into two SMOOTH parts, caps and side band. Every cap vertex touches only cap triangles, which share one normal, so the two big side faces stay dead flat; every band vertex touches only its two neighbouring side quads, so the outline rounds over the way moulded plastic does. That buys flat-looking caps without paying flat shading's per-face vertex duplication.

_round6_screens.negative_result_env_reflection: THE OBVIOUS FIX DOES NOT WORK IN THIS RENDERER, AND IT WAS MEASURED, NOT GUESSED. A dark screen reads as glass in the photographs because it mirrors the room, so the first attempt was a low-roughness / metallic material leaning on scene.environment (a PMREM of three's RoomEnvironment, scene.js) with daylight.js running envMapIntensity to 1.15 in day. Probed on the east run, same pose and crop each time: dielectric roughness 0.06 -> luma 2.08 sd 0.94; metallic 1.0 at #3a3d42 -> luma 1.10; and a PERFECT WHITE MIRROR (#ffffff, roughness 0.05, metallic 1.0) -> luma 8.41 sd 0.69. A perfect mirror is DARKER than round 5's flat slab and carries no spatial variation at all. There is no usable environment reflection on these quads; any future plan that leans on one is dead on arrival.
what_shipped: ar2.SCRN is no longer a self-lit navy slab. Round 5 was #0a0c10 plus emissive #12202c at strength 1.1, and glTF emissive is a flat untextured factor, so every screen in the room rendered as ONE UNIFORM NAVY RECTANGLE - measured luma 18.68, sd 2.18 (11.7% relative), RGB 8.5/20.9/34.1 - brighter than its own bezel and wholly unaffected by the room. It is now a DIFFUSE dark glass, #42464d roughness 0.34 metallic 0.10, with NO emissive at all: a switched-off screen emits nothing, and on the night ramp these panels now go dark WITH the cabinet round them instead of floating out of it.

ar2.crt() (new, sits immediately above upright) replaces the flat screen quad with a 3x3 shallow cap - the same rectangle pushed out along its own normal by bulge*(1-(2u-1)^2)*(1-(2v-1)^2), flush at the rim and 0.06 ft proud at the centre - carrying a vertex-colour grade of (0.66 + 0.34*v) times 0.90 on the rim. That grade IS the gradient: a near-vertical sheet of dark glass in a room with a bright ceiling and a dark floor is brighter across its top and darker across its bottom, which is what v4 6 and v4 7 show. It is a gradient, not a highlight - it names no light source and no specular blob is painted anywhere. The rim darkening is the soft edge shading a tube recessed behind a bezel has.

a2kit.ArtSet.SCREEN, the factor the four painted SOUTH panels print through, went from #3a3a3a plus emissive 0.55 to WHITE plus a small neutral emissive (#16181c at 0.40). Round 5's comment said a white factor would render these as four lit televisions, and that was wrong: art_g2's four panels come out of atlas4 at mean luma 13.0 / 21.6 / 25.7 / 29.4 OUT OF 255 - they are already dark glass. Multiplying them by a dark factor as well rendered Time Crisis's monitor at luma 0.71 and Champion Edition's at 5.17 - black holes - and round 5 only escaped that because its emissive was doing all the visible work, which is exactly what made those four read as switched on.
